articles.title: Vince McMahon and Linda McMahon’s combined net worth in 2026: How WWE power couple builds billion-dollar fortune
articles.summary: WWE News: Vince McMahon and Linda McMahon have spent decades building one of the biggest names in sports entertainment. Their journey began when they were teena.
articles.body: Vince McMahon and Linda McMahon have spent decades building one of the biggest names in sports entertainment. Their journey began when they were teenagers. It eventually led them to the center of the professional wrestling business. Together, they helped turn a regional wrestling company into a global entertainment empire.Vince became the public face of WWE. While, Linda played a major role behind the scenes. She handled important corporate responsibilities. She helped expand the company’s business operations. Their careers later moved in different directions. Linda entered politics and Vince continuing to build his business empire through WWE and other ventures.Vince McMahon and Linda McMahon’s combined net worth in 2026Vince and Linda McMahon have a combined net worth of $3.2 billion, according to estimates cited by Celebrity Net Worth. Their fortune has primarily come from WWE, the company they helped transform into a global sports-entertainment business.A major part of their wealth is connected to TKO Group Holdings. WWE merged with UFC under Endeavor in 2023. This created the publicly traded company TKO. The transaction closed in September 2023.At the time of the merger, Vince McMahon received approximately 28.8 million TKO shares. He later sold a large portion of his stake through several transactions. In June 2025, he sold another 1,579,080 TKO shares to Endeavor for $158.32 per share. The transaction generated about $250 million.After that sale, McMahon retained 6,442,325 TKO Class A shares. At a TKO share price of roughly $192 in September 2026, that remaining stake would be worth around $1.24 billion.Vince built most of his fortune by taking control of his father’s wrestling business. He and Linda acquired control of the company through Titan Sports in 1982. Vince then expanded the promotion nationally and later internationally.WrestleMania became the company’s flagship event. WWE also expanded into television, merchandise, licensing, pay-per-view, streaming and live events. Stars such as Hulk Hogan, Stone Cold Steve Austin, The Rock and John Cena helped make WWE a global entertainment brand.Linda was equally important to the company’s corporate growth. She became president of Titan Sports in 1993 and CEO in 1997. She helped develop merchandising partnerships and oversaw several major business operations.Linda eventually left WWE in 2009 to pursue a political career. She made two unsuccessful campaigns for the U.S. Senate before joining the Trump administration. In 2017, she became Administrator of the Small Business Administration. She left the position in 2019 and later worked on Trump’s political efforts.The McMahons have also held substantial real estate and other investments. Their properties have included homes and luxury apartments in Connecticut and New York.Vince later stepped away from WWE amid investigations into alleged misconduct. He returned briefly in 2023 before resigning from TKO in January 2024 after Janel Grant filed a lawsuit accusing him of sexual assault, coercion and sex trafficking. McMahon denied the allegations.Today, Vince remains a major shareholder in TKO, while Linda’s fortune is closely connected to the wealth the couple has accumulated during their decades in business together.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Deepika's 8-goal blitz powers India to 19-0 thrashing of Uzbekistan at Asian Games
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: India's women's hockey team began their Asian Games campaign in emphatic fashion, cruising to a 19-0 win over Uzbekistan in their opening Pool B match.
articles.body: India's women's hockey team began their Asian Games campaign in emphatic fashion, cruising to a 19-0 win over Uzbekistan in their opening Pool B match here on Sunday.The contest was expected to be heavily one-sided and India lived up to those expectations from the opening whistle, repeatedly breaching an Uzbekistan defence that struggled to cope with the intensity and quality of the Indian attacks.Deepika was the star of the show, scoring eight times in a remarkable individual performance. She found the net in the 8th, 22nd, 25th, 33rd, 36th, 38th, 41st and 54th minutes to lead India's goal fest.Lalremsiami opened the scoring in the seventh minute with a close-range field goal before Deepika added India's second a minute later. Ishika then extended the lead in the 11th minute with a superb first-time finish from the left side of the circle after being set up by Sunelita Toppo.Baljeet Kaur made it 4-0 in the 12th minute, while Neha added another field goal six minutes later.Deepika then took centre stage again, converting a penalty corner with a powerful dragflick into the bottom-right corner. Navneet Kaur followed with a field goal before Deepika struck once more from a penalty corner to send India into half-time with an 8-0 advantage.The onslaught continued after the break, with India adding 11 more goals across the final two quarters.Alongside Deepika's eight, Ishika scored three times, while Lalremsiami, Baljeet, Neha, Navneet Kaur, Lalthantluangi and Sakshi Rana also got on the scoresheet.Ishika struck in the 42nd and 54th minutes after her first-half goal, Navneet added another in the 45th, while Lalthantluangi scored in the 43rd and 51st minutes. Sakshi Rana also found the net in the 43rd minute.The gulf between the two teams was also reflected in the possession and attacking pressure, with Uzbekistan struggling to retain the ball for sustained periods.The match also marked a milestone for veteran India goalkeeper Savita Punia, who earned her 320th international cap. With that appearance, she joined Vandana Katariya as the joint-most capped Indian women's hockey player.Savita had little involvement in the contest, however, as Uzbekistan rarely managed to create meaningful pressure and spent much of the match trying to contain India's relentless attacks.India, the second-highest-ranked side in the competition, will next face Indonesia on Monday.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: China's 13-year-old swimmer Yu Zidi clocks 2:05.08 to break Asian Games record, wins 200m butterfly gold; she also became youngest medallist in World Championships swimming history in 2025
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: China's teenage swimming sensation Yu Zidi completed a memorable Asian Games debut by winning the women's 200m butterfly gold with a new Games record .
articles.body: China's teenage swimming sensation Yu Zidi completed a memorable Asian Games debut by winning the women's 200m butterfly gold with a new Games record in Japan on Sunday.The 13-year-old, who turns 14 next month, clocked 2:05.08 to break the Asian Games record set by China's Zhang Yufei at the Hangzhou Games three years ago. Zhang had won the event in 2:05.57, and Yu finished nearly half a second quicker.Yu crossed the finish line 3.36 seconds ahead of fellow Chinese swimmer Chang Mohan, who took silver.The victory gave Yu her first major individual gold medal and came in the first of the three individual events she is scheduled to compete in at the Asian Games, where the swimming competitiona are being held in Tokyo.Youngest medallist in World Championships swimming historyYu announced herself on the world stage last year when she became the youngest medallist in World Championships swimming history. At the age of 12, she won bronze as part of China's 4x200m freestyle relay team.She also finished fourth in three individual events at the World Championships, narrowly missing out on medals.This year, Yu has continued her rise, including a win over American Olympic champion Regan Smith in March.The schoolgirl, known for her pixie haircut, is expected to be among the contenders at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.Despite her success, Yu has spoken about the pressure that comes with competing at such a young age.Ahead of last year's China National Games, she said the pressure of trying to win the 400m individual medley almost became too much.Her coach encouraged her to keep going and "believe in yourself", she said, as quoted by AFP.Yu went on to win four medals at the National Games.Her rapid rise has also sparked discussion within swimming over the mental and physical demands of elite-level training and competition at such a young age.Under World Aquatics rules, the minimum age for international championships is 14, although exceptions can be made for younger swimmers if they meet the qualifying standard.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ebbw Vale beat Wizards in perfect start to SRC
articles.summary: Ebbw Vale, Newport and Cardiff extend winning starts to the 2026-27 Super Rygbi Cymru campaign.
articles.body:
Ebbw Vale are setting the pace in Super Rygbi Cymru (SRC) after a 52-26 win at Aberavon.

The Steelmen, runners-up in 2025-26, earned a second six-point haul on the bounce when running in eight tries at the Talbot Athletic Ground.

The Wizards led 19-12 at half-time thanks to two tries by wing Frankie Jones after Gavin Parry's opener.

Dragons Harry Rees-Weldon and fellow wing Dafydd Thomas scored in the first half for Ebbw and six more tries followed after the break.

Hookers Ieuan Morris and James Talamai, full-back Morgan Rees (2), Thomas and centre Ethan Phillips all scored, while flanker Rhys Thomas earned the Wizards a four-try bonus point.

Newport are also two wins from two after beating champions Llandovery 46-26 at Church Bank.

The Drovers, who lost their opening fixture at Pontypool, started the better as number eight Daniel Gemine crossed for the opener.

But the visitors dominated the remainder of the half as scrum-half Dafydd Buckland grabbed two tries and wing Oli Andrew, lock Ethan Phillips and flanker Hunter Ward touched down.

Fly-half Ioan Hughes added to Gemine's try for Llandovery in the first half, and they continued their fightback to get the four-try bonus thanks to scores by wing Aaron Warren and replacement back Joshua Thomas.

Newport sealed a comfortable victory - and earned an extra bonus point - thanks to tries by flanker Tiehl Chatham and centre Brogan Leary.

Cardiff are the third team to have won twice after a 49-35 win against Swansea at the Arms Park.

Back-row forward Tirion Bowen, hooker Tom Howe and lock Tom Cottle scored for Cardiff in the first half, but Swansea led 23-21 thanks to wing Brandon Wood's double and a try by centre Jack Hoskins.

Wood completed his hat-trick to stretch the Whites' lead, but Cardiff responded impressively through prop Ioan Emanuel, full-back Isaac Marsh, centre Jason Harries and wing Dewi Cross.

Cardiff were denied an extra bonus point by fly-half Josh Phillips' late try.

Bridgend held off a spirited Pontypool comeback for a 50-38 away win.

The Ravens stormed to a 31-7 lead inside 25 minutes as wing Ben Evans, flanker Tom Jevons, wing McCauley Rowley (2) and centre Ryan Wilkins all crossed, with centre Ryan Conbeer adding a sixth first-half try for the visitors.

Pontypool clawed the score back to 43-38 thanks to tries by locks Liam Antrobus and Dan Hill, flanker Scott Matthews, scrum-half Ellis Lewis, fly-half Evan Lloyd, wing Rhys Cole, but Rowley completed his hat-trick to secure the victory.

Rygbi Gogledd Cymru (RGC) claimed their first win of the season by beating Carmarthen Quins 36-29 in Colwyn Bay.

Prop Pedr Jones, full-back Dion Jones, centre Danny Cross, wing Sam Jones, hooker Osian Burt scored tries for RGC, while Quins left with a pair of bonus points thanks to a penalty with the last kick by Madoc Evans.

articles.title: 76ers 3 goals: Labaron Philon Jr. needs to bring offense to bench unit
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers rookie Labaron Philon Jr. needs to bring offense to a bench unit that will need to support the starters.
articles.body:
In this new series, Sixers Wire looks at the 16 players, per Spotrac , that comprise the Philadelphia 76ers roster — 14 under standard contracts and the two players on two-way deals — and gives each three goals for the 2026-27 season.

The new season begins on Oct. 20, and training camp is right around the corner. Now is the time to begin previewing the new season of adventure that is Sixers basketball.

Up next in this series is rookie guard Labaron Philon Jr., the No. 22 pick of the 2026 draft. The young guard from Alabama averaged 22.0 points, 5.0 assists, and 3.5 rebounds while shooting 39.9% from deep as a sophomore for the Crimson Tide and will be looking to bring that scoring productivity to the league.

For Philon, his three goals are as follows:

The Sixers will have other scorers off the bench to rely on ( Anfernee Simons , for one), but if Philon is to really establish himself in the league, then he will need to find a rhythm early and often. He had his ups and downs in the summer league out in Las Vegas, but the dynamic guard showed off some real potential. He has an ability to really get into the paint, draw defenders, find different ways to finish at the basket up and around defenders, and is able to knock down tough shots. He needs to find that rhythm with the Sixers quickly in order to catch the eye of coach Nick Nurse for rotation minutes.

If there is one real question with Philon, it's his 3-point shot. He saw a big improvement in college, as he went from 31.5% from deep as a freshman on 3.4 attempts per night up to 39.9% on 6.2 attempts as a sophomore, before then shooting just 25.8% on 7.8 attempts in the summer league. He has a smooth shot and has a maniacal work ethic, which will serve him well next to Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe , and that will help him improve along the way. If Philon can come in and knock down 3s at a 34-to-37% clip, then it would be a big help for Philadelphia 's bench unit. He can be a microwave scorer for the Sixers in the long run.

Heading into the 2026 draft, Philon was expected to be a lottery pick. He then tumbled all the way to No. 22 to Philadelphia as it was obvious that there are some teams that have questions about his game. He can prove those teams wrong by bringing that offensive ability to the league right away. If Philon can knock down shots at a consistent rate, get to the basket, and make plays for others right off the bat, then he will be a helpful player right now. If he can become a defensive pest in the future, then he will immediately become a consistent rotation player. He should carry a chip on his shoulder heading into his maiden season.

articles.title: Anthems, transport, housing: What’s gone wrong at the Asian Games in Japan?
articles.summary: Accommodation crisis, transport gaffes and national anthem mix-ups headline the games before their opening in Japan.
articles.body:
A glitzy opening ceremony offered some respite and a more cheerful welcome for athletes and officials attending the Asian Games in Japan after a string of mishaps had dominated the build-up to the continental sporting event.

Five years after the Tokyo Olympics were held at empty venues due to COVID-19 restrictions, Japan welcomed fans to the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium in Nagoya for a curtain-raiser that was initially subdued before bursting into a festival of colour and sound.

Organisers will hope the ceremony can draw a line under a rocky build-up, laden with complaints from athletes and officials involving accommodation and transport.

Hosts Japan bagged the first gold of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games after Takumi Hojo powered to victory in the men’s individual triathlon on Sunday, but not before an eventful opening ceremony made the news for the wrong reasons.

Warnings of a typhoon partly explained why Saturday’s opening ceremony took place in front of thousands of empty seats at the 30,000-capacity stadium.

There was a record deluge last week, which flooded parts of Nagoya. Now, a typhoon is approaching eastern Japan, threatening further disruption in the coming days.

Olympic Council of Asia director general Husain Al-Musallam said they had to keep one block empty because of the games flame, adding that 70 percent of tickets had been sold. However, that contrasted with an announcement at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium that said the ceremony was sold out.

On Friday, Taiwan’s delegation temporarily refused to participate in their welcoming ceremony after sports minister and former Olympic champion Lee Yang was blocked from attending it.

Organisers replaced the traditional games village with a mix of hotel rooms, temporary wooden containers and a cruise ship to house some 17,000 athletes and officials in cost-cutting measures that have gone terribly wrong.

Several national team delegations, including hosts Japan, have found the arrangements below par, complaining of mix-ups and double bookings, while South Korea said the containers at Garden Pier were too cramped for their basketball players.

India’s powerful cricket board took matters into their own hands, arranging for the men’s star-studded cricket team to stay in a separate hotel due to a tight allocation of beds from organisers.

India also leaned on its diaspora in Japan to strengthen their contingency plan, as 2,000 families in Nagoya offered to house the country’s athletes should the accommodation shortage continue.

International Olympic Committee (IOC) president Kirsty Coventry threw her weight behind the games organisers and said she was “really impressed” with the accommodation.

The overarching priority remained ensuring that competitors enjoyed a positive overall experience, the former Olympic swimming champion from Zimbabwe added.

The South Korean men’s basketball team missed a light practice session on Sunday, hours before they were due to take on the hosts in the Asian Games final, after their shuttle bus did not show up at 10am, with team officials saying they had received no explanation.

It was a repeat of what the men’s football team faced on Wednesday, when the bus did not show up at the team hotel. A day earlier, the bus took them to a baseball ground instead of the Mizuho Rugby Stadium, causing a 30-minute delay.

The multi-event games started days before the formal opening.

North Korea anthem played at South Korea match

South Korea’s woes continued as the men’s hockey team were left bemused when North Korea’s national anthem was played instead of theirs before the match against Bangladesh on Friday.

The stadium announcer was quick to apologise for the mistake. The North Korean national anthem is banned in South Korea, along with other symbols of their wartime foes.

articles.title: Two medals in a day: PM Modi, President Murmu hail Elavenil Valarivan's double silver at Asian Games
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday congratulated Indian shooter Elavenil Valarivan after she won the silve.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday congratulated Indian shooter Elavenil Valarivan after she won the silver medal in the women's 10m air rifle individual event at the Asian Games 2026.The two leaders also congratulated Elavenil, Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa K Vinod after the trio won silver in the women's 10m air rifle team event."Hearty congratulations to Elavenil Valarivan on securing Silver Medal in the Women’s 10m Air Rifle Individual event at the Asian Games 2026. articles.title: Asian Games 2026 Day 1: India open medal account with two shooting silvers as hockey, cricket and MMA shine
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: India opened their medal account at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games with two silver medals on Sunday, both coming in the women’s 10m air rifle.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India opened their medal account at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games with two silver medals on Sunday, both coming in the women’s 10m air rifle competition, as Elavenil Valarivan emerged as the standout performer on a day that also brought assured medals, cricket and hockey victories and strong starts in badminton and table tennis.Valarivan first combined with Sonam Uttam Maskar and Games debutant Vidarsa Vinod to win silver in the women’s 10m air rifle team event before adding an individual silver later in the day.The 27-year-old’s individual medal was particularly significant after she had gone without a podium finish in her previous two Asian Games appearances. She shot 252.4 in the final to finish 0.6 points behind Japan’s Hinata Taichi, who claimed gold with an Asian Games record 253.0. South Korea’s Ban Hyojin won bronze with 230.4.For Valarivan, it was a day of both achievement and a near-miss. She had led for much of the final before three loose shots towards the end allowed Taichi to turn the contest around.India’s two shooting silvers provided an encouraging start to a discipline that had produced a record 22 medals at the Hangzhou Asian Games.Suchika assures historic MMA medalWhile shooting provided India’s first medals, Suchika Tariyal ensured another podium finish.The 36-year-old defeated Mongolia’s Altanchimeg Baigalmaa 2-0 in the women’s traditional 60kg MMA quarterfinal to enter the semifinals and assure India of at least a bronze medal.The result assumes added significance with MMA making its Asian Games debut at Aichi-Nagoya. Tariyal, who has previously competed in judo, switched to MMA in 2024 and went on to win gold at the first two MMA-SFI National Championships.She also won bronze at the third and fourth Asian Mixed Martial Arts Championships earlier this year.Shafali century takes India into cricket finalIndia’s women cricketers moved another step closer to defending their Asian Games title with a commanding 114-run victory over Bangladesh in the semifinal.Shafali Verma was the star, smashing her maiden T20I century off just 49 balls as India posted 195/4 after opting to bat. Smriti Mandhana contributed 37, while skipper Harmanpreet Kaur scored 40 off 33 balls.India’s bowlers then bundled Bangladesh out for just 81 in 15.4 overs, with Nandani Sharma and Deepti Sharma claiming three wickets each.The victory secured India a place in Tuesday’s final, where they will face Sri Lanka in a repeat of the previous edition’s gold-medal clash. Sri Lanka defeated Pakistan in the other semifinal.India’s goal rush in hockeyIndia’s men’s and women’s hockey teams made emphatic starts to their respective campaigns, producing a combined 32 goals in their opening pool matches.The women began with a stunning 19-0 win over Uzbekistan, with Deepika Sehrawat scoring a remarkable eight goals.The men followed it up with a 13-1 demolition of Indonesia. Dilpreet Singh led the scoring with four goals, while India dominated virtually throughout the contest.The two victories provided early evidence of India’s ambitions in the hockey competitions and gave both teams a strong start to their Asian Games campaigns.Shuttlers make winning startIndia swept Kazakhstan 3-0 in the women’s team badminton event, with PV Sindhu, Unnati Hooda and Tanvi Sharma all winning their respective singles matches.Sindhu opened with a straight-game victory before Hooda and Tanvi completed the sweep. India did not drop a game in the tie and moved into the quarterfinals, where they will face hosts Japan.The result provided a strong start for a team featuring a blend of experience and youth, with Sindhu leading the charge alongside Hooda and Tanvi.Table tennis: women fight back, men suffer setbackIndia’s table tennis teams experienced contrasting fortunes on Day 1.Both the women’s and men’s teams began their campaigns with identical 3-0 victories over Indonesia in their respective Group F openers.The women then produced one of the day’s notable comebacks, recovering from 1-2 down to beat Singapore 3-2. Yashaswini Ghorpade won the deciding fifth match against Loy Ming, while Sreeja Akula had earlier levelled the contest at 2-2.The men, however, suffered a setback in their second group match, losing 0-3 to Iran. Manush Shah, Manav Thakkar and Harmeet Desai all lost their respective matches.Both Indian teams will next face Pakistan.Heartbreak for Quimcy in teqballIndia’s Quimcy D’Souza came agonisingly close to securing a historic medal in teqball but finished without a podium after losing two bronze-medal matches within five minutes of each other.The 24-year-old pushed Japan’s world No. 7 Yuina Sakamoto to the limit in the women’s singles bronze-medal match before losing 11-12, 11-12.Barely five minutes later, she returned to the arena alongside Mohamed Anas Beg for the mixed doubles bronze-medal match. The Indian pair lost 0-2 to Vietnam’s Hoang Minh Tan Nguyen and Gia Ngih Trinh, going down 9-12, 6-12.Das finishes sixth, other swimmers miss finalsRishabh Das finished sixth in the men’s 100m backstroke final after clocking 54.77 seconds. China’s Jiayu Xu won gold with a Games Record 51.98, while Japan’s Hidekazu Takehara and South Korea’s Juho Lee took silver and bronze respectively.Earlier, Benediction Beniston and Akash Mani failed to progress from the men’s 100m freestyle heats after finishing 12th and 23rd respectively.Wushu brings mixed resultsSuraj Singh Mayanglambam finished 11th in the men’s changquan final with 9.683 points after competing in a 21-athlete field.India also suffered two Round of 16 exits in Sanda. Aparna lost 0-2 to Iran’s Sogand Sinkaeichetan in the women’s 52kg category, while Vikrant Baliyan went down 0-2 to Iran’s Soheil Mousavi in the men’s 75kg category.There was further disappointment in MMA after Varun Sanyal was declared medically unfit to compete following an incident during a sauna session at his cruise-ship accommodation.A medal-winning start with more opportunities aheadBy the end of Day 1, India had two confirmed medals — both silver — through Valarivan and the women’s 10m air rifle team. Suchika Tariyal had assured another medal in MMA, while the women’s cricket team had secured a place in the gold-medal match.The day also delivered emphatic hockey victories, a clean sweep in women’s badminton and a comeback win in table tennis, although the men’s paddlers and some individual competitors endured setbacks.For India, therefore, the opening day brought a mixture of medals, near-misses and promising starts — with several opportunities still ahead as the Aichi-Nagoya Games gather pace.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Iran win Asian Games basketball bronze amid emotional scenes
articles.summary: Players celebrate podium finish that brings exemption from conscription, saying the pressure was ‘out of this world’.
articles.body:
Iran withstood a late fightback to beat China 79-70 and win the Asian Games men’s basketball bronze, an achievement that left their players “speechless” after months of war back home.

China led 31-29 at half-time in Nagoya, but Iran took charge in the third quarter to lead 55-46 going into the fourth and held on to prompt wild celebrations and secure a place on the podium on Sunday.

“To be honest with you, I’m just speechless,” said 6ft 8in (203cm) power forward Arsalan Kazemi, who, in 2013, was the first Iranian to be drafted into the NBA by the Washington Wizards but never made a regular-season appearance.

“The pressure that we had on us is just out of this world,” he added.

“Not a lot of athletes can say that, with the way that it has been for almost six months, what we have been through, what our families have been through.”

“I just congratulate the people of Iran because they deserve much better.”

“And I think my teammates and I put our hearts out on the court today just to get this win and make them happy,” Kazemi said.

Teammate Arman Zangeneh said the squad had been through a lot, but it was worth it.

“If you get the medal at the Asian Games, you don’t need to go to the army any more, so it’s huge for some players,” said the 6ft 6in (198cm) forward.

“We had a very tough two months. We went to the Philippines to play the qualifiers, then immediately we came here.”

“It was really difficult. And living in a container, with the food and everything, it was hard, very hard.”

“In the end, we got to the point where we go home with a medal, and it means a lot,” Zangeneh added.

Male athletes from the country’s national teams who win medals at the Asian Games are granted exemption from mandatory military conscription in a move announced by Iran’s former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in 2018.

Previously, only medallists at the Olympic or world games were exempt from the draft, according to Iran’s semi-official Tasnim news agency.

Iranian males reaching the age of 18 are required to serve two years on active duty and are then transferred to the reserve force.

articles.title: Manu Bhaker wore borrowed kit at Asian Games opening ceremony after ceremonial attire didn’t fit
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: Manu Bhaker wore a borrowed ceremonial kit at the opening ceremony in Nagoya after the kit issued to her did not fit her properly, accordin.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Manu Bhaker wore a borrowed ceremonial kit at the opening ceremony in Nagoya after the kit issued to her did not fit her properly, according to family sources. Her father Ramkishan Bhaker told TOI that even the shoes provided to the Olympic medallist were of the wrong size.“Her shoe size was wrong. Manu wears a 5 number shoe size. The one which was given to her was either 4 or 6. She borrowed the shoe fitting her size,” Ramkishan alleged.Family sources said Manu had received her ceremonial kit, but the size was not right and the jacket did not fit her properly. She eventually wore a kit borrowed from a masseuse attached with the Indian shooting contingent.It is learnt that the masseuse, who is attached to the shooting team through a private sponsor, provided the kit that fitted Manu and which she wore while leading the Indian contingent at the opening ceremony.Family sources said Manu had initially told the National Rifle Association of India (NRAI) that she wanted to focus on her competition, with the pistol events beginning Monday, and concentrate on training and practice. articles.body: NEW DELHI: India ended the opening day of medal competition at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games with two silver medals in shooting, leaving the country joint 10th in the medal standings after a day that also saw assured medals, big wins in hockey and cricket, and encouraging starts in badminton and table tennis.India’s first medals came in the women’s 10m air rifle event, with Elavenil Valarivan playing a central role in both. Valarivan, Sonam Uttam Maskar and Games debutant Vidarsa Vinod combined to win silver in the team event before Valarivan added another silver in the individual competition later in the day.The individual medal was particularly significant for the 27-year-old, who had gone without a podium finish in her previous two Asian Games appearances. Valarivan shot 252.4 in the final, finishing 0.6 points behind Japan’s Hinata Taichi, who won gold with an Asian Games record 253.0. South Korea’s Ban Hyojin took bronze with 230.4.Valarivan had led for much of the final and looked on course to challenge for gold before three loose shots towards the closing stages allowed Taichi to turn the contest around. Despite the disappointment of narrowly missing the top spot, her two silvers made her one of India’s standout performers on the opening day.China lead, Japan close behindChina finished Day 1 at the top of the medal table, collecting 11 gold, six silver and three bronze medals for a total of 20. Hosts Japan were second with six gold, seven silver and seven bronze, also making a strong start on home soil.The Republic of Korea occupied third place with 14 medals, including four gold, while Kazakhstan and Thailand completed the top five. Kazakhstan won three gold and two bronze medals for a total of five, while Thailand’s three medals were all gold.India’s two silver medals placed the country joint 10th at the end of the opening day. The shooting haul also offered an early boost to a discipline that produced a record 22 medals for India at the Hangzhou Asian Games.Beyond the medal tally, India enjoyed several other notable results. articles.title: Hockey India's 'blue' promise goes up in smoke as Indian teams wear saffron at Asian Games
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: The Indian men's and women's hockey teams wore saffron jerseys in their respective opening matches at the Asian Games on Sunday, despite Hockey India'.
articles.body: The Indian men's and women's hockey teams wore saffron jerseys in their respective opening matches at the Asian Games on Sunday, despite Hockey India's pre-event announcement that the teams would return to their traditional blue kits.Both teams wore saffron in their opening matches against Indonesia and Uzbekistan respectively in Kakamilgahara, Japan.The decision comes after the Indian teams, both men and women, had also worn saffron during last month's World Cup in Belgium and the Netherlands, which led to a controversy within Hockey India.Indian hockey teams have largely worn blue jerseys since the country's Olympic debut in 1928, apart from a few isolated occasions.Hockey India president Dilip Tirkey had earlier said that the change in jersey colour was made without the knowledge or approval of the federation's elected leadership and Executive Board. The issue later led to a dispute within the federation, with Tirkey at odds with HI secretary Bhola Nath Singh, who was seen as having pushed for the change in kit colour.However, shortly after the World Cup and ahead of the Asian Games, Tirkey had said that India would return to its blue jersey as the primary kit for the continental event, with white as the other option."The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) had given us options regarding the team kit colours and Hockey India selected blue as the first choice for the Indian team's kit. Orange will be the second choice," Tirkey had said during the send-off ceremony of the Indian contingent for the Asian Games.The teams, however, wore saffron in their opening matches on Sunday.The secondary kits would also not be completely blue, a Hockey India source was quoted as saying by news agency PTI. According to the PTI-quoted source, India will have a combination of white and blue as well as the saffron kit."The two colours for the Indian teams' playing kits for the Asian Games 2026 were always saffron and the combination of white and sky blue, which was approved by the HI president himself.""As to why the president then said that India will wear all-blue at the Asian Games is something you need to ask the president himself," the HI source told PTI.The change in jersey colour was initially explained on the grounds that blue jerseys against a blue turf created visibility problems.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ireland 36-40 USA: Hosts surrender 19-point lead to lose high-scoring WXV opener
articles.summary: The United States stage a remarkable second-half comeback to beat Ireland 40-36 in their WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium.
articles.body:
Tries: Elmes Kinlan, Moloney-MacDonald, Wafer, Higgins, King, Wall Cons: O'Brien (3)

Tries: Perris-Redding, Rogers, Treder (2), Taufoo, Tafuna Cons: Vogel (5)

The United States staged a remarkable second-half comeback to beat Ireland 40-36 in their WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium.

Scott Bemand's side raced into a comfortable lead after 20 minutes following tries from Vicky Elmes Kinlan, Cliodhna Moloney-MacDonald and Aoife Wafer and went in 24-12 ahead at the break.

Erin King added a fifth try early in the second half as Ireland looked to be cruising at 31-12 up, but a loss of control and discipline aided USA, who under the guidance of their Irish head coach Jack Hanratty, managed to turn the game around.

Elmes Kinlan's yellow card was a turning point, with USA taking advantage of their numerical advantage as they scored four successive tries to take an unlikely win.

USA loss 'a game we should have won' - Bemand

Impressive Ireland score four first-half tries

In the first women's rugby Test match to take place at the home of football team Shamrock Rovers, Ireland started with intent and, after persistent pressure, they made the breakthrough on seven minutes.

Bemand's side carved USA open with a slick passage of play as Moloney-MacDonald found Stacey Flood with a quick offload and she drove forward before feeding Elmes Kinlan, who finished in the corner.

Their second try arrived on 14 minutes with Moloney-MacDonald scoring off the driving maul before Wafer then forcing her way over soon after to further extend their advantage.

The Eagles, who were without Ilona Maher, responded well after that tough start and co-captain Georgie Perris-Redding got them on the scoreboard as she bundled over on 25 minutes, with teenager Bella Vogue nailing the conversion.

Ireland re-established their comfortable lead just two minutes after USA's try as Anna McGann galloped forward and offloaded to Eve Higgins to dot down, with Dannah O'Brien adding the extras.

USA came again at the other end and the experienced Hope Rogers crashed over after patient play to narrow the gap again before the break.

Ireland started the second half as did the first and added a fifth try soon after the restart.

Robyn O'Connor darted forward and Erin King eventually grounded the ball with the try awarded after a TMO (television match official) review.

Ireland then dropped off and USA capitalised with Kathryn Treder scoring after peeling off a driving maul from the line-out.

Elmes Kinlan was then sent to the sin-bin for not rolling away quickly enough from a tackle and USA punished the hosts.

Treder was again on the scoresheet with a carbon copy of her first try and USA then edged in front for the first time on 69 minutes as Hallie Taufoou forced her way over with Vogel accurate from the tee to give them a two-point lead.

With momentum on their side, the USA pressed home their advantage with Freda Tafuna scoring the pick of their tries as she held off a number of Irish players before diving over.

Dorothy Wall got a late try for Ireland as the clock ticked into red, but they were unable to add another with their last attack of the game as USA turned the ball over and held out for a fine win.

Bemand's side will now look to bounce back in their next game against Japan in Galway on 27 September.

articles.title: González Fuertes: "Hay temeridad en la entrada de Cuti, pero no es roja porque no hay suficiente intensidad"
articles.standfirst: El analista arbitral de Radio MARCA considera acertada la decisión de Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias
articles.summary: El analista arbitral de Radio MARCA considera acertada la decisión de Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias
articles.body: En el minuto 37 los jugadores del Real Madrid recriminaron a Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias que mostrara la roja a Cuti Romero por una entrada sobre Bellingham. Así lo valoró Pablo González Fuertes en el programa 'Marcador' de Radio MARCA. "El muestra la amarilla a Bellingham y hay un error claro de identidad porque la entrada es de Romero sobre el jugador del Real Madrid. La acción no es de roja. Existe temeridad, peor no hay intensidad suficiente, por eso está bien sancionada con amarilla". El encuentro entre el Atlético de Madrid y el Real Madrid comenzó con una enorme intensidad táctica y disputas constantes en el centro del campo. Ambos conjuntos saltaron al césped con la clara intención de adueñarse de la pelota, provocando numerosas interrupciones por faltas en los primeros minutos de juego. La jugada más polémica del primer tiempo llegó cerca del descanso, cuando Álex Baena protagonizó una entrada sobre Bellingham que encendió todas las alarmas en el banquillo merengue. Los futbolistas madridistas reclamaron de forma inmediata la tarjeta roja directa para el jugador rojiblanco al considerar la acción desmedida. Tras revisar las imágenes detenidamente en la pantalla del VAR, el colegiado decidió finalmente cancelar la revisión de la expulsión y mantener la amonestación en tarjeta amarilla. La controvertida resolución permitió al centrocampista continuar en el partido, desatando fuertes protestas antes de que los equipos se retiraran a vestuarios.

articles.title: 'This medal means more than my life': Suchika Tariyal's emotional reaction after creating history at Asian Games
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: Suchika Tariyal assured India of its first Mixed Martial Arts (MMA) medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games after defeating Mongolia's Altanchimeg Baiga.
articles.body: Suchika Tariyal assured India of its first Mixed Martial Arts (MMA) medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games after defeating Mongolia's Altanchimeg Baigalmaa 2-0 in the women's Traditional MMA 60kg quarterfinal on Sunday.The victory took the 36-year-old into the semifinals, where a place guarantees at least a bronze medal as both losing semifinalists receive bronze. Suchika will face Singapore's Teo Hui Hoon in Monday's semifinal.MMA is making its Asian Games debut at Aichi-Nagoya 2026.After the quarterfinal win, Suchika said the medal meant everything to her after years of hard work and sacrifice by her family.“This medal means a lot to me as me and my coaches have worked very hard to reach here. My family has spent a lot of money for me and provided me with every possible support to help me become a good MMA player. So, this medal means more than my life,” Suchika said in a video posted by Sports Authority of India.Suchika said the level of competition at the Asian Games is different because many professional fighters are part of the field.“The competition at the Asian Games level is very high as mostly pro level players compete here. The scoring also is different as you can’t use knees and elbows. Sometimes it helps too as it gives time to recover. If you get hit on the face, you are knocked out. The chances of injuries are a bit less but it is a very technical sport. Amateurs and professionals both are playing so it is a bit tough.”Earlier this year, Suchika was included in the Sports Ministry's Target Asian Games Group (TAGG) scheme. She also received support for her domestic training before the Asian Games at One Punch Academy in Mumbai, along with equipment support for kits, training and recovery.A native of Rohtak in Haryana, Suchika comes from a modest and conservative family. She took up judo at the age of 12 after an incident of eve-teasing, learning the sport as a form of self-defence.Suchika went on to become an eight-time national judo champion and won several international medals for India. She won gold at the 2019 Commonwealth Judo Championships and the 2019 South Asian Games.At the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham, she competed in the women's 57kg category and narrowly missed a medal.She made her MMA debut in 2017 with a win before taking a seven-year break from the sport while continuing to compete in judo and jiu-jitsu. articles.title: Kenya’s Ngetich breaks women-only half-marathon world record by a second
articles.summary: Agnes Ngetich finished 50 seconds ahead of compatriot Veronica Loleo, who came second.
articles.body:
Kenya’s Agnes Ngetich took a second off the women-only half-marathon world record on Sunday when she won the World Athletics Road Running Championships in Copenhagen, stopping the clock at one hour, five minutes, and 15 seconds.

Ngetich, who also broke the women-only 10km (6.2-mile) world record last year, pushed to the front from the outset on a sunny morning in the Danish capital and led until the end, finishing 50 seconds ahead of compatriot Veronica Loleo, who came in second.

The previous record was set by Peres Jepchirchir, another Kenyan, when she won the World Half Marathon title in Poland in 2020.

The overall women’s half-marathon world record is held by Ethiopia’s Letesenbet Gidey, who clocked 1:02:52 in 2021 at the mixed-gender Valencia Half Marathon in Spain.

Sunday’s win was the latest major title this year for the 25-year-old Ngetich, who also won the team half marathon in Copenhagen and the World Cross Country Championships in Florida in the US in January.

articles.title: 'Los Gallos' ganan en Ginebra y ¡suman su octavo podio de la temporada!
articles.standfirst: El equipo español de SailGP se impuso en la final a Australia, Dinamarca y Suiza. Se consolida en la segunda plaza del Rolex SailGP Championship. Sólo faltan dos citas antes de la Gran Final
articles.summary: El equipo español de SailGP se impuso en la final a Australia, Dinamarca y Suiza. Se consolida en la segunda plaza del Rolex SailGP Championship. Sólo faltan dos citas antes de la Gran Final
articles.body: El equipo español de SailGP está protagonizando la mejor temporada desde que compite en la Fórmula 1 del mar. Aunque ganó en 2024 el título, nunca había sumado tantos podios en una misma campaña demostrando una regularidad impresionante. Este domingo se ha impuesto en el Gran Premio de Suiza en el lago Lemán y suma ya su octavo podio de la temporada (3 victorias, 2 segundos y 3 terceros) en 11 Grandes Premios. Y en dos de ellos (Perth y Nueva York) no pudo competir por problemas técnicos del F50. Sólo les queda la espinita de Valencia. Diego Botín, Florian Trittel, Joel Rodríguez, Nicole Van der Velden, Joan Cardona y Bernardo Freitas quieren coser la segunda Copa en su camiseta. Con esta victoria, 'Los Gallos' dan un paso importante hacia la Gran Final de Abu Dabi (29 de noviembre) al consolidarse en la segunda plaza del Rolex SailGP Championship (78 puntos), por detrás de Australia (94). Además, amplía su ventaja respecto al Artemis (59), tercero. Todo a falta ya sólo de dos Grandes Premios antes de la Gran Final que disputan los tres mejores de la temporada. El poco viento hizo que el sábado no se pudiese disputar la tercera regata de flota del Grupo A, compuesto por Estados Unidos, Dinamarca, Alemania, Suecia (Artemis), Francia (DS Automobiles), Brasil y 'Los Gallos' españoles. Por eso, este domingo comenzó con la celebración de la prueba cancelada, aunque se tuvo que recortar el recorrido. 'Los Gallos' se llevaron la victoria de una carrera cuya salida fue caótica, con sanciones para Alemania, Brasil y Dinamarca. Estados Unidos, con la brasileña Martine Grael a los mandos, fue el equipo que mejor salió pero los de Botín apostaron por la ruta costera y la estrategia dio sus frutos hasta arrebatar la primera plaza a EE.UU. España se colocaba líder del Grupo A, con solo un punto de diferencia entre los equipos que ocupaban los puestos del segundo al quinto. Estaba al rojo vivo. En la cuarta regata de flota, Francia hizo una salida impecable mientras que 'Los Gallos' salieron sextos. Tocaba remontar. ROCKWOOL Racing presionó bien y acabó llevándose la victoria gracias a una penalización a los franceses por un error garrafal al cruzarse con los daneses sin tener prioridad de paso. España remontó un puesto y con la quinta plaza sumó un punto que le mantenía en la lucha por entrar en la final. Y en la quinta y última regata de flota, antes de la final a cuatro entre los dos mejores de cada grupo, 'Los Gallos' lograron un valioso tercer puesto, por detrás de daneses y suecos que le dio el pase a su octava final de la temporada. Por parte del Grupo B, los mejores fueron los Bonds Flying Roos australianos y los Explora Swiss, que mantenían el sueño de coronarse campeones en casa. Llegó el momento de la verdad. Los Bonds Flying Roos protagonizaron una salida fantástica en la final, pero con 'Los Gallos' al acecho. Cara a cara entre los dos pesos pesados de SailGP. Los primeros son los ganadores de las tres primeras temporadas y líderes actuales de la general del Rolex SailGP Championship. Los segundos, campeones de la cuarta temporada y segundos en la general. Los dos mejores equipos frente a frente. La tripulación de Diego Botín logró arrebatar la primera plaza a la de Slingsby y ya no la soltó hasta cruzar la línea de meta casi juntos. ¡Campeones en Ginebra! Se recuperan de la decepción de haberse quedado fuera de la final en Valencia hace dos semanas. La próxima cita será ya en Dubai el 20 y 21 de noviembre y después, los días 28 y 29 de ese mes en Abu Dabi. Allí, se celebrará la Gran Final el día 29 entre los tres mejores. El ganador se llevará 2 millones de dólares como premio.

articles.title: Blaney, Hocevar React to Wild Fight on Video After Crash at Bristol During NASCAR Chase
articles.summary: Carson Hocevar and Ryan Blaney both offered their sides after their confrontation Saturday night at Bristol Motor Speedway.
articles.body:
Carson Hocevar and Ryan Blaney both offered their sides after their confrontation Saturday night at Bristol Motor Speedway.

Hocevar threw a pair of punches at Blaney before the pair were separated. Blaney managed to break free and got off a strike of his own.

"There wasn't a whole lot of talking," Hocevar said, per the Associated Press . "He just kind of said one thing and then went after me, and I wasn't going to take it. I got ran into a lot for the win. That was for second, and he wants to come fight. They got an old-school Bristol show here."

Blaney clearly took exception to contact from Hocevar late in the race. He had to settle for a 33rd-place finish despite leading 202 laps and winning Stage 2. The result knocked him down to sixth in the overall standings .

In an interview immediately after heading back to the garage, Blaney didn't blame Hocevar outright, but his frustration was evident:

This may have been an accumulation of things, too, because Hocevar's driving style has earned him few friends on the circuit.

"I haven't had a problem with him for probably a year and a half, but it's getting old," Blaney told reporters .

Hocevar, for his part, didn't think he was at fault for the pivotal crash.

"I don't know what I did wrong there," he said. "I crossed him over and looked like he spun himself, and then he wants to instigate a fight. I was going to finish that, and it seemed like the crowd was pretty pumped up, so I was going to play the audience for a second."

The stakes are high enough for the Hollywood Casino 400 at Kansas Speedway next week. Blaney and Hocever's fight will provide another subplot.

articles.title: Oregon Ducks open as road favorites vs. USC Trojans
articles.summary: Oregon heads into hostile territory this week as slim favorites against rival USC.
articles.body:
With Week 3 now in the books, the Oregon Ducks can turn their attention to Big Ten play. The Ducks got back on track after blasting Portland State , 84-0, on Friday night, but the competition gets much tougher this week on the road against the USC Trojans.

The Trojans remain undefeated heading into the matchup, while the Ducks are hoping to pick up a marquee victory after losing to Oklahoma State in Week 2. FanDuel Sportsbook released an early line last week that favored the Ducks as the road team in Los Angeles. After the games played out on Saturday, the number has gotten even bigger.

Oregon is now favored by 2.5 points against the Trojans, also sporting -128 odds on the money line. USC survived a close call against Rutgers on the road, winning 42-35, and that helped boost the total points line up one point to 61.5 points. Given what both defenses have shown so far this season, it's fair to assume the Ducks and Trojans will both put up plenty of points next Saturday.

The Ducks covered the spread for the first time this season on Friday, covering a massive 58.5-point spread against the Vikings. Oregon played the starters in the first half, in which Dante Moore tossed four touchdowns, before mixing in the backups and letting Dylan Raiola make a stellar debut in Eugene .

Both USC and Oregon are battling significant injuries that are worth monitoring this week and could ultimately impact the point spread. The Trojans are hoping to get back defensive tackle Jahkeem Stewart , who has yet to play this week, and freshman wideout Trent Mosley is also dealing with an injury. Oregon played on Friday without tight end Jamari Johnson , wideout Jeremiah McClellan and corner Carl Williams IV , all of whom enter the week with an unknown status.

Dan Lanning is 2-0 against Lincoln Riley since they took over their respective programs before the 2022 season. Both of those wins came in Eugene, including a 42-27 victory last November. There is plenty on the line this time around, both in terms of national title hopes and recruiting efforts in Southern California.

Oregon and USC will play in the national spotlight as well. The game is set to kick off at 4:30 p.m. PT and will air live on NBC.

Getting a plate of hot chicken is one of the culinary highlights of a trip to Nashville, but Sunday in the city is going to be focused on a lot of hot Eagles and Titans.

Weather forecasts call for a high of 97 degrees in Nashville on Sunday with a heat advisory in place from the National Weather Service that warns the heat index will rise above 105 degrees.

The Eagles tried to prepare for the intense heat at practice this week. Cameron Wolfe of NFL Media reported that the team's offensive linemen wore hoodies to practices in order to simulate the kind of conditions they will face when they are on the field at Nissan Stadium.

The temperature could test the depth on both sides of Sunday's matchup and the team that manages the conditions better could find themselves with an edge come the fourth quarter in Nashville.

articles.title: Ian Rapoport shares positive injury update for Seahawks QB Sam Darnold
articles.summary: Perhaps we could be seeing Darnold back on the field sooner than later!
articles.body:
The biggest storyline surrounding the Seattle Seahawks revolves around the health of starting quarterback Sam Darnold , who was lost five plays into their Week 1 game. Seattle ended up winning 13-10 over the Patriots due to their stifling defense and backup quarterback Drew Lock , who will be taking the helm for the next few weeks.

Darnold is dealing with a unique soft tissue injury that doesn't necessarily have a concrete timeline, but the 12th Man may have received some good news. On Sunday morning, NFL insider Ian Rapoport shared a positive update about Darnold progressing with his recovery quicker than was initially thought. Darnold is still expected to miss the Week 3 road game against the Washington Commanders , but their Week 4 home showdown against the Los Angeles Chargers appears to be within a realistic return window for him.

The full segment from Rapoport can be seen below.

For now, the Seahawks will be rocking with Drew Lock. Darnold has already been ruled OUT for the Week 2 game against the Arizona Cardinals . Despite Arizona winning last week over the Chargers, I do believe the Seahawks are in a great position to survive a game or two without Darnold.

Drew Lock is a capable backup, and it will be fascinating to see what a full week of practice can do for him and this Seattle offense.

Murray is expected to clear the concussion protocol early this week. If he doesn't have a setback, all signs point to him taking over as Minnesota 's starting quarterback in Week 3 against Tampa Bay.

Carson Wentz is starting at quarterback today, and J.J. McCarthy is the backup. McCarthy led the Vikings to a thrilling victory at Soldier Field in Week 1 last season.

articles.title: What Florida's Jon Sumrall said after beating Auburn in SEC opener
articles.summary: Here's everything that Florida football head coach Jon Sumrall said after the Gators beat the Auburn Tigers on the road in Week 3's SEC opener.
articles.body:
The Jon Sumrall era continues its hot start after Florida football beat the Auburn Tigers , 44-39, on Saturday night. For the first time since 2007, the Gators put up 40-plus points in their first three games as the offense continues to impress.

However, it was not all sunshine and rainbows inside Jordan-Hare Stadium, as Sumrall's squad showed some struggles on defense, while problems with the penalty flag reared their ugly head. There is still plenty of headroom for improvement, but it was still an encouraging showing from the Orange and Blue in its SEC opener.

Following the big road win, Sumrall spoke to the media about his team's performance against the Tigers. Here is what he had to say.

PHOTOS: Top highlights from Florida vs Auburn in Week 3's SEC opener

Alright, no bad wins. Always good to win. We still have a lot to improve upon. That's not our best football. We're going to get there. So much to work on, to improve.

The penalties were out of control. I mean, 16 penalties, we won't win another game all year if we do that again. Not one more game. And so I got to get it cleaned up, as a staff got to get it cleaned up, got to play more disciplined. I didn't agree with all of them, but still I'm not gonna let our guys off the hook; that's inexcusable.

But man, I grew up in this state. As a kid, there was a couple people I always watched, and one of his name's on this field, Pat Dye. Like, I got a ton of respect for Pat Dye, God rest his soul. And then the other two across the state — Gene Stallings and Bear Bryant — like, I watched those guys my whole life and Bear Bryant died basically when I was born but I've idolized the great coaches that have coached in this state. And for our first SEC win as a program with me as a head coach to do it on Pat Dye Field, I can't tell you what that means to me personally, because I've got a picture of Pat Dye and Bear Bryant in my office in Moundville, Alabama, hunting rabbits, and to do it on Pat Dye Field means something to me.

But this is about our guys; I'm so proud of them. They found a way. A lot of people doubted them. I heard a lot of people all week second-guessing why we were favored in this game. It didn't have to be as close as it was. They're well-coached, they're a good football team, wish them nothing but the best, and excited to get back on this plane and get back home and get to work tomorrow.

Was being able to run against Durkin's offense a concern ahead of the game?

I knew we were going to do what we did on offense tonight. Hey, I've watched them enough to know how we were going to play on offense. The interception, we gave them a gift, didn't need to give that to them, but I had no doubt how we were going to play on offense.

Like, the people that were concerned about how we're going to play on offense — I'm probably more concerned about our defense holding up to be honest with you, but offensively, I knew we were going to run the ball on them, I knew we were going to throw the ball on them. They're good up there, but I felt like we were better. I felt like the matchup leaned our way.

Jadan Baugh did a great job responding. That really unfortunate play, should have caught the ball — bad, bad, bad play. I grabbed him and I said, "Hey, around here, when something bad happens, we say good, and when something good happens, we say good," and so I went over to him after the play and I said "Hey, good, you got a chance to redeem yourself now, go make another play next time." I didn't like it, but that's our mindset: when something bad happens, we say good.

I don't know if we played with poise. I mean, I thought we responded — that's what I thought we did. I think if we played with better poise, we wouldn't have had the dumb penalties we had. I do think we showed them we have some mental toughness and we're resilient, but I don't think we played with poise all the time.

I think our responses were good. Anytime they countered, we had a couple jabs left in the left, you know what I mean? Like, we kept responding all night. So I don't know if we played with the poise I need to see us play with if we feel like we're where we need to go, but I do think our response was really good.

On Philo's first road start in an SEC environment

I thought he handled it really well, you know. He's got a little bit of, like, a cowboy mentality, man. Like, he's tough as nails. He don't talk a whole lot just to talk, he ain't that type of dude, but he ain't gonna back down or nothing. Like, I can tell watching him, just how he carries himself, I got a lot of confidence and our team has a lot of confidence in him, just because that's the way he's wired. He's a tough, blue-collared, chip-on-your-shoulder type of guy.

On Emmanuel Oyebadejo's performance considering the week he had

Yeah, he was a true game-time decision. Him and E (Eric Singleton Jr.) were both. I think we'll have a real good shot at getting E back next week. But Emmanuel really only ran around a lot on Friday, and never really fully practiced all week and was very questionable going to the game, and so proud of him showing up and playing with the toughness he did.

Huge, huge. Like, that's what I talk about. We made responses. I don't know that we played really clean, but we responded in some big moments where you had to go make a play.

On keeping Byrum Brown in the pocket, limiting his ability to have unscripted plays

I thought for the most part we did a good job. A little bit leaky at times. The thing that I was not pleased with was we felt like with him, the type of passer he was, we needed to stay on the top shoulder of the route all night and try to force him to make intermediate or short game throws, and we did not do that at times.

But the run game, really the couple he got, really, we just didn't stay in our rush lanes. But most part you felt us push the pocket, get frontal on him and not allow him to be real comfortable.

On Sumrall's confidence that they'll clean up the penalties

We better. I'm not confident yet, because we haven't done it. You know, we played really good football Week 1 penalty-wise; we had four in week one. Then we had eight last week. We had 16 (tonight), so I'm not a mathematician, so four to eight's doubling them, and eight to 16 is doubling them again.

If we don't get that fixed and get back to how we were in Week 1, we are about to get absolutely embarrassed when we play high-end SEC teams.

This week, the conversation was really three words: work the cut. Alright?

So I don't know how familiar you are with boxing or UFC, but Justin Gaethje came and talked to our team back here in training camp. And I showed them pictures of Gaethje's fight against (Ilia) Topuria in DC, the White House lawn this year. And everybody thinks you knocked the other guy out by just a big hit. That's not how it happens.

In fighting or anything in a game, man, you have to cut the eye. And then you keep cutting the eye with the jab. And then at some point you wait for the uppercut. But you don't start with uppercuts; you wear the guy down, and I think that was really on the headset all night — when something good would happen or bad would happen — I'd go to the all-call button and say, everybody, tell the guys, "Work to cut. Work the cut. Work the cut. Work the cut." And eventually, if we keep working the cut, we'll find ourselves victorious.

They got a couple punches in on us too. Like, they bloodied our eye a couple times, too. But we were the last man staying.

On the photo with Bear Bryant and Pat Dye, hunting rabbits

They were hunting rabbits, yes. They're in Moundville, Alabama, in a hunting camp, getting ready to go hunt rabbits. They were eating rabbit soup or rabbit stew. I got the picture in my office. It's a, you know -- I grew up in a state. I love football. I love that football has been played in the state forever. Like, at both schools and all schools, at Troy.

Like, I love Troy football, man. And so I've idolized Pat Dye, Bear Bryant, Gene Stallings my whole life. And so, yeah, they were hunting in Moundville, Alabama. Alabama people here don't even know where Moundville, Alabama, is, but I do, because I'm from the state. But it's a picture I cherish because I love great football coaches and I have a lot of respect for both of those guys.

On if Sumrall liked the team's confidence pre-game

I knew our guys were ready, but yeah. Like, I might have used some motivation from outside people that had said, like, we weren't really as good. We hadn't played anybody. That's what I heard a lot of from like, some people out in the media. We hadn't played anybody. I think FAU is pretty good. I think Campbell was a decent football team. But they talked about how they had played people.

Well, they played us tonight. And so we were going to be ready to play the game the way we needed to play it. It still wasn't good enough to go win the big ones we got coming. We were able to win this one. We turn the page tomorrow to the next one. If we play like that, we will get just slaughtered. It won't even be close. So we've got a lot to work on.

But I think our guys were mentally prepared to come on the road, take the challenge, hostile environment, great crowd, backs against the wall a little bit. Like, a lot of people against us and play with the demeanor of being a good, tough football team.

On the up-and-down defensive performance

"Well, yeah, it goes back to — if we would just do our job and stay on top of the coverage. Like, I might, I'm not going to throw this table. I said it at media days: I was going to throw the podium or something.

We did not, at times, do simple things that we were coached to do. Like, stay on the top shoulder. We just dive to the low hip and I'm like, "Well, that's not what we've talked about. Just do your job." And so until we are so on point with everybody doing their job all the time, we're going to give up stupid explosive plays like we did the night that were not necessary.

And they made, credit to them, they made some plays. But like, there's a couple of them out there that we just decided to give them a gift. And that's not what good football teams do.

On interviewing for the Auburn head coach job

Who said I interviewed for this job? What are you talking about? I didn't interview. They didn't want me, I didn't want them.

On Buster Faulkner's halftime adjustments

We felt good coming into the half about some things we could do to attack them off of some things we had seen. It's huge to set the tone early. I do think that was really the game-deciding, if you will, swing back and forth of like, how we came out of the locker room the start of the second half.

I felt like we were a little bit more dialed in maybe than we had been the whole game, to be quite honest on both sides for a minute there. So I thought it was a huge sequence for sure.

On how momentum continued into the second half

Yeah, I just thought our guys played with confidence. You know, if we don't get the holding penalties late in the game there — like I said, I think we stopped ourselves, but it was nice to see us respond coming out of halftime. Sometimes you worry about starting the second half in a lull, or maybe a lethargic vibe, and our guys didn't have that at all offensively. Or really defensively to start the half.

"I do want to say another thing. Kayla Beckley, John Beckley's wife. John Beckley worked for me at Troy — he was a GA for me; he's now coaching at Tulsa. His wife passed, young, like 30. Really young, recently, and, you know, while I'm celebrating a win tonight, there's people that do this that have real lives and family.

And John Beckley, a dear friend of mine, somebody I Iook at really closely because he worked for me when I was head coach at Troy, lost his wife recently, and way too young. Just want to acknowledge a lot of the guys that coach with him wore yellow ribbons tonight. I didn't make a big deal out of it, but we're thinking of them during this tough time. So thank y'all.

USA, led by County Dublin-born head coach Jack Hanratty, fought back from trailing 31-12 at one stage of the second half to score four successive tries and claim a 40-36 comeback win.

A loss of discipline in the second half contributed to Ireland's loss after their impressive first-half display, and Bemand was frustrated that they let the game slip out of their control.

"We came out of the blocks, moved the ball well and got momentum and showed our style of play. USA then got some momentum using their power game and we've got to be a bit cuter and smarter in stopping teams getting that momentum," he told TG4.

"When teams get momentum the penalty count is more likely go up. There's bits we can control, not from a discipline perspective but in terms of our technical process, how we can be faster finishing tackles and getting break down pressure."

USA stun Ireland with comeback WXV win in Dublin

A late try from Dorothy Wall as the clock ticked into red gave Ireland the chance to snatch a late win, but they were unable to add another with their last attack of the game as USA turned the ball over.

While pleased with the resilience shown from his side to keep fighting to the end, Bemand was disappointed that they were forced to scramble for a late winner having cruised through long periods of the game.

"You never expect our girls to give up but it's a shame we put ourselves in that position," he added.

"It's a game, I'm not saying we would have ever romped home on the scoreboard, but I think we'll look at it and think it's a game we should have won.

"How we rally at the end, you don't want to find yourselves in a position to do that."

Next up for Ireland is two games against Japan, one in the WXV in Galway next weekend and another in Cork at the start of October, and Bemand is hoping for a strong response.

"Every time we have issued a challenge to our players they've responded. We need to get 80-minute performances, having a good 40 minutes isn't what we're about," he added.

"It's two more opportunities to show what we can play like. [I'm] really excited with how we can take our learnings today and go and come back better."

articles.title: LSU football news: Why Lane Kiffin said 'you're welcome' to Ole Miss after wild return
articles.summary: LSU head coach Lane Kiffin initially planned to approach his highly anticipated return to Oxford like any other game. However, the emotional experience prove...
articles.body:
LSU head coach Lane Kiffin initially planned to approach his highly anticipated return to Oxford like any other game. However, the emotional experience proved to be overwhelming following a tough 32-24 loss to his former Ole Miss program. Kiffin admitted that the six years filled with life-changing moments and deep connections made the hostile environment more challenging than he had anticipated.

While reflecting on the chaotic atmosphere and the electric energy from the Rebels' fans, Kiffin made a sharp and humorous comment about the intensity of the stadium. In his postgame remarks, a report from On3 highlighted Kiffin's reaction to the atmosphere at Ole Miss, where he quipped, "I guess I had to leave to get them to do that. You're welcome." This witty remark captured the surreal nature of a night during which he faced relentless boos and a deafening crowd that finally matched the elite standard he had spent years trying to establish in Oxford.

The celebration continued even after the final whistle, as the home crowd added insult to injury for the visiting Tigers. To top off the 32-24 victory, the Pride of the South marching band delivered a memorable musical jab at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium by playing "Neck," one of LSU's most iconic tradition songs, while fans celebrated on the field. Between Kiffin's sarcastic gratitude for the crowd's peak energy and the marching band's unforgettable performance, the Tigers' return to Oxford culminated in a dramatic finish that will be remembered in SEC lore for years to come.

articles.title: Former England international gets run over by pitch roller in bizarre Thai league incident
articles.summary: Former England international Andros Townsend escaped serious injury after being run over by a pitch roller in a bizarre incident at a Thai league match.  Tow...
articles.body:
PATTANI, Thailand (AP) — Former England international Andros Townsend escaped serious injury after being run over by a pitch roller in a bizarre incident at a Thai league match.

Townsend currently plays in Thai League 1 for PT Prachuap and made headlines on Saturday night when a clip emerged on social media that showed the 35-year-old being taken out by the vehicle during a warmup for the game against Pattani.

The former Tottenham and Crystal Palace winger saw the funny side, reposting the video on his Instagram account with the words "Make it look like an accident" and a laughing emoji. He also joked about the incident on his stories.

Screams were heard on the video and other players could be seen turning away and putting their hands on their head in shock.

The incident happened as Townsend attempted an aerial backheel and landed in the path of the vehicle, just as the driver appeared to look away. Townsend was run over by the roller, which continued to move over his legs and hip.

Townsend avoided serious injury and even managed to come on as a stoppage-time substitute in his team's 3-0 win.

Townsend, who made 13 appearances for England, joined Prachuap in August from another Thai club, Kanchanaburi Power, which had just been relegated.

articles.title: Duke 35, Stanford 7: Position grades for the Blue Devils
articles.summary: Duke improved to 3-0 on the season with a 35-7 rout of Stanford as Nate Sheppard ran for 154 yards and three total touchdowns.
articles.body:
Duke improved to 3-0 with a 35-7 rout of Stanford to open ACC play on Saturday in Wallace Wade Stadium.

The Blue Devils relied on another big game from Nate Sheppard (154 rushing yards, three total touchdowns) and a massive defensive effort to shut down the Cardinal and start their bid to repeat as conference champions.

Walker Eget made some big throws, especially on a third-quarter touchdown drive that helped give Duke a 21-7 lead, but he was still inconsistent at times, completing just 14-of-24 passes. The Blue Devils will need better play from him soon.

Nate Sheppard continued to show why he's one of the best players in college football, while CJ Campbell came through with some hard-hitting runs in relief.

Jeremiah Hasley has become Eget's favorite target, and for good reason. The tight end caught five passes for 88 yards, including a long reception on 4th down that helped set up a touchdown.

It was nice to see Jared Richardson and Jaivon Solomon catch a few passes.

No sacks on Eget, and the big guys up front paved the way for 268 rushing yards and four touchdowns on the ground against a defense that prides itself on stopping the run.

Tyshon Reed had a huge game, recording four tackles, two tackles for a loss and two sacks as the Blue Devils consistently hounded Stanford quarterback Davis Warren.

Kevin O'Connor was everywhere as well, putting up two sacks, two tackles for a loss and forcing a fumble.

Nick Morris staying healthy has helped this unit, as he brings leadership and productivity. He recorded five tackles on Saturday, while Kendall Johnson recovered a fumble.

Still prone to giving up big plays, although the longest reception for the Cardinal on Saturday was just 22 yards. Dylan Flowers led the Blue Devils with seven tackles.

Kade Reynoldson averaged 49.4 yards per punt, with a long of 60 yards. Cosme Salas had an easy day, converting on all five point-after attempts.

It would have been easy for the Blue Devils to overlook Stanford following last week's win at Illinois , but Diaz and his staff had the team ready to play and made sure they came out excited with the surprise onside kick to start the game.
