articles.body:
TreVeyon Henderson is officially back. The second-year running back, who missed the New England Patriots ' season opener in Seattle because of an ankle injury suffered in late August, is part of his team's game day roster for Week 2: he will make his season debut against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday.

Henderson returned to practice on Monday and by Wednesday was already listed as a full participant . Two days later, he was off the injury report and set to return. Sunday's inactives list, which is six players deep, confirms the comeback.

As for those inactives, they look as follows:

The Patriots entered Sunday with two players unavailable: offensive tackle Dametrious Crownover and cornerback Carlton Davis were both already ruled out for the contest due to their respective knee and neck injuries. Joining them on the list are four healthy scratches.

Behren Morton and Walter Rouse were already inactive for last week's game against the Seahawks . Tanner Arkin and Leonard Taylor, meanwhile, have lost their spots on the game day squad.

The biggest names on Pittsburgh's inactives list have already been known: cornerback Joey Porter Jr. and wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. were both ruled out heading into the game. Whereas the former is officially dealing with conditioning and back issues — "contract dispute" is traditionally notlisted on the practice report — the latter is out for Week 2 with a foot ailment.

Kickoff between the Patriots and Steelers at Gillette Stadium is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET .

articles.title: Rangers flip narrative as McInnes makes mark
articles.summary: Consecutive Old Firm derby wins show Derek McInnes is starting to make his mark at Rangers after a mortifying start.
articles.body:
"I like putting my name to this team at the minute," Rangers manager Derek McInnes said after a second Old Firm derby win in a week.

That is hardly surprising, given the Rangers side that won 1-0 at Celtic Park in the league after last Sunday's 3-0 win at Ibrox in the League Cup is starting to look like a team built in McInnes' image.

A sluggish start to the campaign resulted in humiliating exits from the Europa League and Conference League and raised alarm bells among Rangers fans as they fell off the pace set by Celtic. The team looked completely lost.

Now, it is showing the hallmarks of its manager as they clinched a sixth straight victory and back-to-back derby triumphs to narrow the gap to Celtic to two points.

"Take it back a month when Derek McInnes was under real pressure," former Rangers midfielder Andy Halliday said on BBC Scotland's Sportsound.

"A big thing that was quite confusing to people is: 'it doesn't look like a Derek McInnes team'. They don't look organised off the ball, they don't look aggressive, they don't look athletic.

"How that narrative has completely changed over the last three, four weeks. That for me is a Derek McInnes team, what we watched today.

"Front foot, aggressive, making contact with people, when they win the ball back playing forward, running forward and putting Celtic under constant pressure for large parts of the game."

McInnes conceded he is still "embarrassed" by the European exits against Jagiellonia Bialystok and Jablonec and said the criticism was hard to respond to earlier in the season.

But he has shown over 800 games as a manager that he can organise and motivate a team to be difficult to beat off the ball.

His Hearts side which went so close to winning the league last season conceded the fewest of any team in the Premiership. Rangers have conceded just once now in their last six games, having kept just one clean sheet in their first seven this season.

Dujon Sterling , playing in his best position of right-back, has formed a physically imposing unit with Emmanuel Fernandez and Olwethu Makhanya inside him.

That trio's defensive solidity allows James Penrice to maraud forward from left-back and help Rangers add numbers to their midfield.

Fernandez still has lapses in concentration. He was lucky not to be sent off at Celtic Park after an early booking for hauling down Camilo Duran was followed up by a dodgy challenge on Benjamin Nygren which went unpunished.

But once he settled, he repelled everything that came into Rangers' box, making 11 clearances. Makhanya next to him brings calm authority and was named man-of-the-match. Celtic were restricted to one shot on target at home.

In front of them, Dan Neil and Nico Raskin have stepped up in midfield. The pair made the most passes in Rangers' ranks, always showing for the ball and getting stuck in.

Rangers made 75 fewer passes than Celtic overall, but 50 more than their rivals in the opposition's half. While Celtic's passes were often between centre-backs, Neil and Raskin found each other and players in more advanced areas.

"My midfield were terrific again," McInnes said. "Celtic filled the midfield. We filled it with even more bodies, we just made sure we weren't going to get overrun in there.

"We look far more calm, far more settled in everything that we're doing. The players deserve so much credit for that."

When captain Lawrence Shankland pulled a hamstring against Motherwell having just started scoring regularly, it only raised concerns around Rangers.

Could Naderi and new £9m signing Kevin Kelsy fill the void? The former failed to wholly convince last season after a January switch from German third-tier side Hansa Rostock.

Now, he has four goals in 13 games, more than he managed in the second half of last season. His goal at Celtic Park was what Rangers will want more of.

Lurking to pounce when Kim Min-su's shot was parried out to him, he got his knee over the ball and finished smartly. But aside from his goal the 23-year-old German helped set the tone.

He was involved in an astonishing 34 duels, 18 of them in the air. He won 11 of them and worked so hard he was still panting for breath in his post-match interview.

To add to his physical presence, he had the most shots and touches in the Celtic box.

"His all round play was really, really good," former Rangers striker Kris Boyd said on Sky Sports. "Him and [Kevin] Kelsy didn't have much link up play but they were working together. If one went short, one went long.

"Naderi's running power was really key for Rangers. When he came in at first there was a rawness about him. But there is a lot to like.

"If Derek can get a hold of him and work with him and make him that complete striker, because he works his socks off and he can finish."

McInnes knows given the record investment in this Rangers squad, these sort of performances and results will be expected every week, especially without the burden of European football.

At an average age of 24, though, Rangers have one of the youngest groups in the league, and being shorn of their experienced captain Shankland only adds to that sense of rawness.

Former Rangers winger Peter Lovenkrands said on BBC Radio Scotland that the team will take "so much confidence" from beating their rivals twice in a row.

McInnes agrees this has to be the starting point, but becoming the first Rangers manager since Graeme Souness to win his first two derbies gives him a strong platform.

"There's a lot of growth in the team," the Rangers boss said. "And winning in places like this only helps. But there's plenty of league games to be won and we have to concentrate on that.

"It was hard to defend the criticism [at the start of the season]. We're on a strong run now, six wins in a row, which is the kind of consistency we're searching for.

"But at the start we didn't look ready, for whatever reason, we didn't look settled as a team, didn't carry an attacking threat.

"But we've knuckled down and worked hard, and hopefully that winning habit is something we can keep working towards."

articles.title: Listen to the Vanderbilt football radio call for improbable win over NC State
articles.summary: Hear the Vanderbilt football's radio call for its win over NC State on a fumble recovery touchdown.
articles.body:
Andrew Allegretta is glad he pressed record on Sept. 19 in the FirstBank Stadium radio booth, even when the Commodores were given just a 0.1% chance of winning in the final seconds of their game against NC State .

Vanderbilt (3-0) pulled off the improbable comeback when Miles Capers forced a fumble and Cayden Daniels recovered in the end zone with one second left and the Wolfpack (1-2) leading by three. It was only the second time in the last 20 seasons when a team lost when leading with the ball in the final 10 seconds of the game.

Inside Vanderbilt football vs NC State, Jared Curtis' first start

Allegretta, the play-by-play radio announcer for football, posted his final call of the 35-31 win on his social media.

"Did they knock the football loose? Oh goodness, did Miles Capers get the football?" Allegretta says, after initially believing that NC State quarterback CJ Bailey had taken a safety by getting sacked in the end zone.

"Touchdown! Touchdown!" analyst Norman Jordan says.

'Unbelievable. You've got to be kidding me. One of the most improbable finishes in the history of Vanderbilt football," Allegretta says.

Following the play, Vanderbilt had to hold for several more minutes to officially confirm a win. First, replay upheld the fumble, then one second was added back onto the clock, requiring the Commodores to kick the extra point and then kick off into the end zone. The Wolfpack made one final pass attempt after Vandy's kickoff went into the end zone. That pass was completed and included multiple laterals before the ball was fumbled back to the Commodores to end the game.

articles.title: Mizzou Football Opening Odds: Tigers head to Starkville for SEC opener
articles.summary: Mizzou opens conference play against confident, rising Mississippi State.
articles.body:
Do you hear the sound of cowbells? Calling us south?

Mizzou's 27-17 win over Troy wasn't an inspiring way to end non-conference play. But as Eli Drinkwitz pointed out in his post-game conference, winning college football games is hard. And it's about to get a lot harder, with Mizzou headed to Mississippi State for an SEC opener that suddenly looks a lot tougher than it did a few months ago.

While many of us would have fancied Mizzou's chances over a Bulldogs team that has struggled in recent seasons, the emergence of Kamario Taylor changes the equation. The sophomore QB looks like the real deal these days after leading his team to a 41-34 comeback win at South Carolina . He's sporting an 11-1 touchdown to interception ratio and a whole lot of confidence as the Bulldogs try to fight their way out of the SEC cellar. So no pressure, right? Just go into an SEC stadium and humble the upstart star signal-caller. Easy.

FanDuel seems to agree that the task isn't so simple, as they have Mississippi State as -3.5 favorites to open their Week 4 books. Personally, I'm a bit surprised it's that low. Mizzou hasn't looked overly convincing in any of its games thus far, and going to Starkville to open conference play is tough sledding. Still, Mizzou has elite talent where it matters. If they want to get that first CFP bid, going on the road and winning at Mississippi State is a must.

articles.title: Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany has full belief in Jonas Urbig
articles.summary: FC Bayern might have a star in the making.
articles.body:
Vincent Kompany is not exactly shy when it comes to discussing Jonas Urbig 's potential.

With the young Bayern Munich goalkeeper receiving a call-up to Germany's senior national team, Kompany offered a remarkably confident assessment of where he believes Urbig's career is heading. The Bayern Munich boss made it clear that he sees the goalkeeper as much more than a promising backup for the future.

"You also have to plan for the future. If anyone thinks Jonas won't become number one in Germany, they're making a big mistake. He'll certainly be Germany's number one at some point. It's a sensible, very sound decision. Jonas has the right mentality. As a country, you have to develop your talent," Kompany said (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ).

That is quite the endorsement from Kompany, particularly considering the competition Urbig faces for the Germany No. 1 spot.

Marc-André ter Stegen currently has the job under Jürgen Klopp, while Germany also has several other young goalkeepers pushing for opportunities. Urbig, however, has already earned the trust of Kompany at Bayern Munich and continues to develop alongside experienced goalkeeping figures such as Manuel Neuer .

For Kompany, the Germany call-up is about more than simply rewarding Urbig for his recent progress. It is part of developing the next generation of German talent. Whether Urbig eventually becomes Germany's No. 1 remains to be seen, but Kompany clearly believes the Bayern Munich goalkeeper has the mentality and ability to reach that level.

articles.title: Howie Rose bids farewell to fans on one of last Mets broadcasts of his career
articles.summary: For nearly four decades, Howie Rose has been broadcasting New York Mets games on the radio. On Saturday, he called what could possibly be his final game. The...
articles.body:
For nearly four decades, Howie Rose has been broadcasting New York Mets games on the radio. On Saturday, he called what could possibly be his final game.

The Mets beat the Philadelphia Phillies 10-3 on Saturday evening and will close out the four-game series on Sunday afternoon. But Rose officially put a bow on his legendary career last night, hedging against a poor weather forecast for Sunday that threatened to postpone the Mets' final home game of the season.

"Whether they play tomorrow or not, I just preemptively want to say how much you all mean to me," Rose told listeners during Saturday's postgame show. "And when I'm saying 'you all,' it's not a dialect, it's covering not only my friends here in the booth and my colleagues, but right now I want to speak solely to you, the Mets fan. Because I've used the term forever, kindred spirits, and I think you understand that any one of you could be where I'm sitting here in this booth because we have very similar backgrounds. I grew up in the upper deck of Shea Stadium, many of you sit in the upper deck here or sat somewhere here or at Shea Stadium. But the point is that I feel like I know you, and more importantly I feel like that you know me. But what I feel more than anything is that we've been together for the entirety of my time in this booth. And if I ever doubted that or ever thought that maybe that was an exaggeration, believe me, it's hit home over the last couple of weeks with all the intention that this retirement announcement has somehow gotten. …It's been ridiculous. It's been so overwhelming, I just feel like it's a bottom of an avalanche with it.

"When I really reflect on it, I have to basically quote the best to ever do it, and that's Vin Scully. And I guess if you're going to plagiarize anybody, you might as well plagiarize the best. …He spoke to the fans and he said, 'You know, I needed you more than you ever needed me.' And I didn't understand that when he said that, but reading the comments and everything that's been written, whether that be newspapers, online, broadcast, anywhere else, to hear the love that you've sent to my family and me, I think I know what Vin meant."

On Sunday morning, the Mets announced that the team's planned ceremony to celebrate Rose will be postponed to the start of next season, though the game will be played as scheduled.

"Howie Rose is more than a broadcaster to this organization. He is a part of the fabric of the New York Mets. Out of respect for everything he has meant to our fans, we have decided to postpone the ceremony and instead honor him during Opening Weekend 2027," President of Business Operations Lew Sherr said in an announcement on Sunday. "While we are disappointed that inclement weather will prevent us from having our planned ceremony, we want to make sure that we properly celebrate Howie for all that he has done for the Mets."

Rose would appear to be in line to call Sunday's contest, giving him one final opportunity to say farewell to fans. Rose, however, did not close the door to an occasional return post-retirement, saying last month he could drop in for a game or two after he retires.

articles.title: Chicago Cubs vs. Cincinnati Reds preview, Sunday 9/20, 12:40 CT
articles.summary: The Cubs will try to clinch a postseason spot.
articles.body:
SPLITTING THE DIFFERENCE, AGAIN: This is the 24th of the Cubs ' 51 series in which they have split the first two games. There was no third game in one series. In the others, the Cubs are 10-12 overall and 6-7 on the road. They ae 6-6 after losing, then winning, including 5-2 on the road. (Courtesy BCB's JohnW53)

THE DIFFERENCE IS LIKE NIGHT AND DAY: The Cubs are only 33-33 in day games, compared to 53-36 at night. They are 10-17 in day games on the road, but 8-9 in day games on the road following night games. The Cubs have finished with a losing record in day games only once in the last 10 full seasons: 2021, at 32-39. They were 33-41 in 2014. (Courtesy BCB's JohnW53)

KEEPING THE BALL IN THE YARD: Cubs pitchers have not allowed a home run in the last three games — their longest homer-free streak of the season! They had had back-to-back games five times before: March 31-April 1, April 7-8, May 30-31, July 24-25 and July 28-29. They had played 44 games from July 30 through last Tuesday without going two games again. (Courtesy BCB's JohnW53)

WALK WATCH: The Cubs drew three walks Saturday, giving them a season total of 650. They need seven more to break the franchise record of 656, which was set in 2016.

RUN WATCH: The five runs the Cubs scored Saturday gave them 826 for the season, or 5.33 per game. If they continue at this pace for the seven remaining games, they will score 863 runs, which would be the most for any Cubs team since 1930.

David Peterson's last two starts were very good — just two runs allowed in 10.2 innings, with 11 strikeouts.

He also threw well against the Reds Aug. 28 at Wrigley Field , allowing two runs in five innings. Then the bullpen came in and made a mess of things, so don't click on that boxscore link. Don't say I didn't warn you.

Peterson also faced the Reds twice this year as a member of the Mets , one start and one multi-inning relief appearance. Don't look at those, either. Hopefully, today will be better.

Rhett Lowder was Peterson's opponent in that Aug. 28 game. The Cubs scored three runs in five innings off him, including a home run by Michael Busch .

Since then, in three September starts Lowder has an ERA of 11.68 and a 2.108 WHIP and… bring your bats, Cubs hitters.

articles.title: The NFL will make a decision on any potential discipline for Jed York ‘soon’
articles.summary: 49ers owner Jed York will miss the home opener to avoid any distractions
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York will miss his second game in a row, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. York didn't make the trip with the team to Australia and will now miss the 49ers' home opener.

He's staying away to avoid any distractions, per Schefter. York pleaded to two misdemeanor charges on August 24 after being arrested in Ohio. He was arrested last month on suspicion of engaging in prostitution .

According to Columbiana County court records in Ohio, York allegedly responded to an undercover ad on a known prostitution website where he "arranged to have sexual activity with a female in exchange for $140."

The original prostitution charge was amended to misdemeanor disorderly conduct as part of the plea agreement resolving the case. The other misdemeanor was possessing criminal tools, which wound up being York's cell phone.

Schefter said the NFL is expected to make a decision on any potential discipline for York "soon." Back in August, around the time the incident occurred, the NFL said it was "aware of the matter, which will be reviewed under the personal conduct policy."

articles.title: Littler threatens Dutch boycott after booing before sweep bid ends
articles.summary: Luke Littler has threatened to boycott tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled during the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam. Th...
articles.body:
Luke Littler has threatened to boycott tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled during the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.

The back-to-back world champion faced a hostile environment during Friday's win over home favourite Danny Noppert and it escalated on Saturday night as referee Charlie Costorphine had to intervene in the last-16 win over Nathan Aspinall.

Littler has taken a stance against volatile crowds before, refusing to travel to European Tour events in Germany as a result of his treatment from fans there.

And he is "100%" prepared to do the same in the Netherlands.

"With the Germans, I haven't been for a long time, we will have to see in Dortmund whether it changes or stays the same," he told Online Darts.

"If the Dutch stay like this, then I'm not going to do any Euro tours over there. There's just no point in me travelling, wasting my time whilst I'm getting booed.

"I just want to play my darts, obviously sign autographs.

"The past two nights, I've done nothing, I've just walked off stage without thanking anybody. There's no point thanking everyone when they are booing me."

Despite the bearpit atmosphere, Littler came out on top in a last-leg decider with Aspinall to keep his dream of a clean sweep alive but it ended on Sunday when he was beaten 10-4 by Jonny Clayton in the quarter-finals.

The 19-year-old was aiming to become the first man to win all 10 major televised tournaments in a calendar year, having triumphed in the first five.

Clayton completed the win with a checkout of 40 to set up a semi-final tie with Gerwyn Price on Sunday evening.

Ross Smith will face Gian van Veen in the other last-four match for a place in the final, which will be over the best of 21 legs.

articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans might log their hottest home game in franchise history against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sept. 20 (noon, FOX).

Heat indexes could reach the triple-digits, so fall is not in the air.

But that didn't stop Titans running back and special-teamer Julius Chestnut from looking toward Halloween — again. He arrived at Nissan Stadium wearing a Marvel Green Goblin costume, one week after wearing a Black Panther costume to the season opener.

articles.title: Michael Carrick details why one Red is unavailable for Fulham v Man Utd but stays tight-lipped on one absentee
articles.summary: Michael Carrick is without two players who featured in Manchester United’s midweek defeat to Brighton and Hove Albion.Indeed, Ayden Heaven and Benjamin Sesko...
articles.body:
Michael Carrick is without two players who featured in Manchester United's midweek defeat to Brighton and Hove Albion .

Indeed, Ayden Heaven and Benjamin Sesko have both been omitted from the matchday squad.

Why Benjamin Sesko is unavailable vs Fulham

Speaking to the media ahead of kick-off, Carrick confirmed that Sesko had felt a slight injury following the Carabao Cup tie, so he decided it was best to leave him out this afternoon.

"A little bit of an assessment at the moment. He pulled up after the game the other day with a little bit of pain, so we'll have to see how he is," said the manager.

The Slovenian is United's only out-and-out centre-forward in the side this season, but he has still yet to start a Premier League fixture, with his only two starts of the term coming in the League Cup and Champions League.

Ayden Heaven dropped from squad at last minute

(Photo by Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

Elsewhere, Ayden Heaven is nowhere to be seen on the teamsheet, despite being fit and available.

He travelled with his teammates to London, but will travel back at full-time without playing any minutes in the clash with the Cottagers.

It's thought that his absence is due to Carlos Baleba being deemed match-fit on the day of the game, hence his inclusion on the bench instead.

Heaven did oversee a particularly dismal display in the loss to the Seagulls, so he was presumably in line to lose his starting spot anyway.

After this weekend, fans will have to wait three weeks to see United back in action due to the lengthy international break.

Their first outing in October comes on the 10th, when they take on winless Tottenham Hotspur at Old Trafford in a 5.30pm kick-off.

articles.title: USA loss a game Ireland 'should have won' - Bemand
articles.summary: Ireland head coach Scott Bemand says their defeat against USA in the WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium was "a game we should have won".
articles.body:
Ireland head coach Scott Bemand said their defeat against USA in the WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium was "a game we should have won".

USA, led by County Dublin-born head coach Jack Hanratty, fought back from trailing 31-12 at one stage of the second half to score four successive tries and claim a 40-36 comeback win.

A loss of discipline in the second half contributed to Ireland's loss after their impressive first-half display, and Bemand was frustrated that they let the game slip out of their control.

"We came out of the blocks, moved the ball well and got momentum and showed our style of play. USA then got some momentum using their power game and we've got to be a bit cuter and smarter in stopping teams getting that momentum," he told TG4.

"When teams get momentum the penalty count is more likely go up. There's bits we can control, not from a discipline perspective but in terms of our technical process, how we can be faster finishing tackles and getting break down pressure."

A late try from Dorothy Wall as the clock ticked into red gave Ireland the chance to snatch a late win, but they were unable to add another with their last attack of the game as USA turned the ball over.

While pleased with the resilience shown from his side to keep fighting to the end, Bemand was disappointed that they were forced to scramble for a late winner having cruised through long periods of the game.

"You never expect our girls to give up but it's a shame we put ourselves in that position," he added.

"It's a game, I'm not saying we would have ever romped home on the scoreboard, but I think we'll look at it and think it's a game we should have won.

"How we rally at the end, you don't want to find yourselves in a position to do that."

Next up for Ireland is two games against Japan, one in the WXV in Galway next weekend and another in Cork at the start of October, and Bemand is hoping for a strong response.

"Every time we have issued a challenge to our players they've responded. We need to get 80-minute performances, having a good 40 minutes isn't what we're about," he added.

"It's two more opportunities to show what we can play like. [I'm] really excited with how we can take our learnings today and go and come back better."
authors: Lauren McCann - BBC Sport NI Journalist
